items.titleZh: 宏碁掠夺者Helios Neo 16S AI评测：轻薄OLED游戏本，续航不给力
items.descriptionZh:
宏碁Predator Helios Neo 16S AI是一款主打“轻薄化”的高性能游戏本，试图回应部分用户既想要便携、又不愿放弃高规格游戏硬件的需求。该机采用曜石黑、棱角分明的Predator家族设计，机身尺寸14.05×10.85×0.74英寸、重4.85磅，在游戏本中相对轻薄；但为容纳后部散热架，机身深度比技嘉Aero X16和HyperX Omen 15多约1英寸。机身与顶盖为冲压铝材，刚性尚可但容易沾染指纹。接口是其亮点：提供Thunderbolt 4、3个USB-A 3.2、USB-C 3.2、HDMI 2.1、2.5Gbps以太网、MicroSD读卡器和音频接口，后置接口便于理线；无线为Killer Wi-Fi 6E AX1675i，并支持Killer Doubleshot Pro双网络连接，可将游戏流量与其他应用分流。核心配置为Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus处理器、Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti（12GB GDDR7、最高115W图形功耗）、16GB DDR5-6400双通道内存、1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD，以及16英寸16:10 OLED屏，分辨率2560×1600、刷新率240Hz并支持G-Sync。售价为2774.99美元，另有32GB内存版本标价3199.99美元，评测期间曾打折至2459.99美元；宏碁官网还列出2099.99美元的RTX 5060版本，但未找到实际销售。

评测的核心问题是：这款较薄的游戏本能否在便携的同时保持稳定游戏性能。答案是基本可以，但前提是插电使用。其RTX 5070 Ti最高115W，明显高于对比机型技嘉Aero X16和HyperX Omen 15的85W RTX 5070，加上更新的Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus，整体游戏表现显著领先。在《007 First Light》中，2560×1600原生分辨率、高画质并开启DLSS时，多数场景约65—75 FPS，开阔区域可超过100 FPS，整体可玩。对比测试中，《古墓丽影：暗影》最高预设下1080p为125 FPS，与HyperX的126 FPS接近，但在原生1600p下以76 FPS领先技嘉的60 FPS和HyperX的64 FPS；《孤岛惊魂6》Ultra原生分辨率下为122 FPS，对手分别为85和107 FPS；《赛博朋克2077》光线追踪Ultra原生分辨率下为21 FPS，对手为17和5 FPS；《极限竞速：地平线6》Extreme下1080p为72 FPS，低于HyperX的80 FPS，但原生分辨率下以60 FPS反超HyperX的51 FPS；《荒野大镖客2》Medium下与技嘉接近，原生分辨率为52 FPS对49 FPS。总体看，它在2560×1600原生分辨率下具备合格且稳定的游戏能力，后部散热架换来的机身深度使其GPU功耗更高，是性能优势的重要原因。Metro: Exodus 15轮压力测试中平均86.82 FPS，轮间波动不足1 FPS，CPU的P核平均2.94GHz、E核2.16GHz、平均温度73℃，GPU平均1.622GHz、74℃，显示持续散热较稳定。

生产力方面，Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus表现强劲：Geekbench单核3349、多核19313，明显高于Ryzen AI 7 350的2916/14074和Core Ultra 9 386H的2857/15916；Handbrake 4K转1080p耗时2分30秒，对手为3分54秒和3分39秒；25GB文件传输平均2034.84 MBps，对手为1480.57和999.57 MBps。16GB内存会限制重度多任务，但该机支持选购32GB版本，且可后期升级。屏幕是重要卖点：OLED面板色彩鲜艳、黑色纯净、 glossy表面观感通透，2560×1600兼顾细节与RTX 5070 Ti可驱动的游戏负载，240Hz和G-Sync提升流畅度；DCI-P3覆盖82.7%，与技嘉相当但不及HyperX OLED，SDR峰值亮度372.4尼特，40% HDR测试可达608尼特。不过屏幕仅支持240Hz、不能降至60Hz或可变刷新，成为续航偏短的主要原因。

键盘手感良好，键程与缓冲充足，MonkeyType测试首次达到116词/分、99%准确率；加号上方按键可通过Acer Key自定义，四区RGB而非单键背光，可在PredatorSense中设置多种灯效。触控板面积大、点击可预期、表面顺滑。音频是短板：掌托两侧双扬声器音量仅够 casual listening，清晰度一般、低音薄，游戏时定位尚可但建议使用耳机，DTS:X均衡器设为Auto效果较好。可升级性方面，底部10颗T6螺丝且卡扣较难拆，侧通风口与底盖一体增加难度，但内部提供两个SODIMM插槽、一个M.2 2280 SSD位、一个M.2 2230无线网卡位，电池也可更换。续航令人失望：92Wh电池在150尼特、Wi-Fi网页浏览/OpenGL/视频流测试中，HyperX多出近2小时、技嘉多出近2.5小时；对轻薄游戏本而言这是讽刺性短板。表面温度在Metro压力测试中，键盘G/H键间峰值103°F，触控板81°F，底部中心129°F；游戏时风扇可闻，日常使用安静。1080p IR摄像头画面较清晰、高光处理合理，无物理或电子隐私快门，但支持红外人脸识别。

软件方面，PredatorSense提供安静、均衡、性能、Turbo功率模式、系统监控、更新和设置；性能模式称会超频CPU/GPU但未说明细节，Turbo疑似性能模式加风扇满转；可禁用Nvidia Optimus、设置优化电池充电、蓝光护盾、30秒键盘背光超时，风扇可自定义RPM但无曲线，场景配置可保存灯效和均衡器。预装软件偏多，不少只是微软商店链接；Acer Intelligence Space提供会议助手、图像生成、媒体搜索和可自动改变准星颜色的游戏助手等AI功能，可能有用，但同时存在McAfee试用、Dropbox推广和《Forge of Empires》等臃肿软件，对如此高价机型并不合适。

综合来看，Predator Helios Neo 16S AI兑现了多数“轻薄游戏本”承诺：RTX 5070 Ti在漂亮的240Hz OLED屏上提供扎实游戏性能，键盘触控舒适、接口实用、升级性不错；但续航低于平均，削弱了便携意义，游戏风扇噪音和扬声器表现也是妥协。它更适合在多个可插电地点之间携带、以游戏和生产力为主且能接受插电使用的用户；若追求真正长续航的移动游戏体验，则需谨慎考虑。

items.title: Lawyer builds private AI server with eight used Nvidia V100 GPUs
items.description: A lawyer runs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on eight used 2018-era Nvidia V100 GPUs at up to 215 tokens/s, keeping case files in the office.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 12 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A lawyer posted on Reddit about their private AI server built from eight used 2018-era Nvidia Tesla V100 data center GPUs so case files never have to leave the office. With two 4-card SXM2 NVLink boards, four PEX switches, and SlimSAS cables everywhere — plus one burnt power connector — the builder now runs the open DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model with every expert in GPU memory, at up to 215 tokens per second. The four-GPU boards cost about $2,400 apiece when the builder bought them.Lawyer's V100 homelab, update: two 4-card SXM2 NVLink boards, four PEX switches, SlimSAS everywhere, one burnt power connector, and a 250 GB model running entirely in VRAM at 200+ tok/s from r/homelabThe eight Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB cards, each with 32GB of HBM2 at 900 GB/s, plug into SXM2, Nvidia’s mezzanine socket for data center GPUs, rather than PCIe slots, and are split across two baseboards. Inside each board, all four cards are NVLinked — NVLink is Nvidia’s direct GPU-to-GPU link — for 128GB per board, but the two boards only communicate over PCIe. Each board connects to the host through two PEX (PLX) switch cards over SlimSAS cables, four switches in all, with each switch handling two GPUs at PCIe 3.0 x8 speeds over its own x16 uplink.The given prices are already in the past, though: used V100 SXM2 32GB cards are now listed on eBay for about $900, more than double the roughly $400 apiece from the post, and listings suggest prices are still climbing. The system also already has some other necessary components: a Gigabyte Threadripper Pro motherboard with a 12-core 3945WX CPU to match, 8x 32GB DDR4 RDIMM, one NUMA node, and two PSUs, 2,800 W in total, are on separate regular office circuits. This is a real-world case for used data center hardware as a cheap route to getting lots of fast VRAM together in one place.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The server is currently in daily use for first-pass work on case files: it reads a folder of records, pulls out facts, dates, and numbers, summarizes them, and takes a first swing at routine drafting. “Nothing goes out the door without a real review,” which is a good human-in-the-loop policy in general. It also helps ensure privacy for cases where client files can’t be sent to a cloud or frontier model. RAG databases and tool calls are wired in; the operator can drive the system through a Discord-style interface over SSH, in this case from a Windows PC. For now, it handles only one request at a time.DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is compressed to mostly 2 bits here, and its weights still total 248.8GB. The model’s “experts,” the parts that do most of the work for each word, live entirely in GPU memory, while about 110GB of lookup tables, called Engram tables, stay in the system’s regular RAM. Fetching from RAM costs about 0.12 milliseconds per step, which the builder says barely affects the speed numbers. You may like Reddit user pays $35 for a crypto mining rig left in a garage and gets 54GB of VRAM at 65 cents per GB Firm rents four Nvidia H200s to test '80x cheaper' DeepSeek claim Homelabber uses second-gen Optane memory sticks to run a 2.8-trillion-parameter AI model on CPU alone The first half of the model’s layers (0–19) runs on the first SXM2 board and the second half (20–39) on the second. Each board handles its heavy traffic over its own NVLink, so only one hand-off per step has to cross the slower PCIe link between the boards. In an earlier post, the builder found that splitting every layer across all eight cards made speeds “fall off a cliff” because of that PCIe hop.Performance is surprisingly good for a model this size. Code comes out fastest, at up to 215 tokens per second, because a small draft model built into DeepSeek guesses five tokens ahead, and code is easy to guess. Legal writing, which is what the server is for, runs at up to 118 tokens per second.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsLong documents take longer to get going: the model reads prompts at about 2,200 tokens per second, so at 128K tokens, the first token arrives after about a minute. It can accept up to 524K tokens of context. Three days before the post, the same model on four of these cards managed just 36–38 tokens per second. The jump came with the second board, which could presumably double performance under ideal circumstances, and the builder credits custom kernels and prefill work for the rest. See the table for the full breakdown. Swipe to scroll horizontally DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on eight Tesla V100s, by prompt length Prompt length Wait for first token Code (tokens/s) Legal writing (tokens/s) 1K tokens 1.2 seconds 215 118 32K tokens 17.2 seconds 200 117 128K tokens 59.2 seconds 183 111 256K tokens 118.7 seconds 160 103 Builder’s measurements, Nov. 5; greedy decoding, 1,024 tokens out, mean of two runs.It wasn’t as simple as hooking everything up and turning on the power. The host reset itself twice with a fatal PCIe error on the link to one GPU board, both times with a higher power limit and uncapped GPU clocks. In this state, the cards drew 192–232 W, past the 180 W limit. The best guess, although “not proven,” is that a board stops responding during load spikes. What to read next Nvidia PAIR utility joins every GPU in your home into a cluster for agentic AI tasks Beijing AI bar that offers unlimited free DeepSeek coding tokens with $1.50 drink haemorrhaging cash Benchmarking Qwen 3.8 27B on RTX 5090 and beyond The resets stopped after the builder capped the clocks and removed one board whose power connector had a burn mark; “Check your connectors, people.” Each card is now capped at 150 W, half of its 300 W rating, with the graphics clock capped at 1522 MHz. A 200 W cap brought no appreciable performance gains, according to tests.The system memory hit uncorrected ECC errors, too, which went away after the builder dropped the RAM from DDR4-3200 to DDR4-2666. One GPU was connected at x4 instead of x8 at last check, and the builder plans to reseat it; one commenter traced the same kind of problem on their own V100 to a bad cable.The pain was worth the payoff as an estimated 50–60% of the lawyer’s existing LLM workflows can now run on the box instead of frontier models. Helping bridge the gap is a second DeepSeek server on two DGX Sparks, where the two systems hand work off to each other. The setup does appear to save money, at least when compared to API pricing, although the builder says it’s not really faster. However, it will protect client data “once it is self contained, which is the goal.”The builder added that the V100 box might also get a 240 V circuit. Beyond power, the system is also on borrowed time with the Nvidia R580 driver branch, which is the last to support Volta. For now, the lawyer admits that it’s mostly a hobby, but in the future it may be a business idea. The next step is to handle two or three requests at once, something built and checked on a test system but not yet on the server. items.titleZh: 律师用八块二手Nvidia V100 GPU搭建私有AI服务器
items.descriptionZh:
一位律师在Reddit上分享了一套私有AI服务器：用八块2018年时代的二手Nvidia Tesla V100数据中心GPU搭建，目的是让案卷文件完全不离开办公室。这套系统由两块4卡SXM2 NVLink基板、四个PEX/PLX交换机以及大量SlimSAS线缆组成，搭建过程中还遇到过一个烧毁的电源连接器。它目前运行开源的DeepSeek V4.1 Flash模型，所有“专家”参数都放在GPU显存中，最高可达215 tokens/s。 builder购买时，每块四GPU基板约2400美元。

硬件方面，八块Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB每块拥有32GB HBM2显存和900 GB/s带宽。它们使用Nvidia面向数据中心GPU的SXM2夹层插槽，而不是PCIe插槽，并分装在两块基板上。每块基板内四块卡通过NVLink直连，每板聚合128GB显存；但两块基板之间只能通过PCIe通信。每块基板通过两个PEX交换机卡经SlimSAS连接主机，四个交换机各负责两块GPU，以PCIe 3.0 x8连接GPU、以x16上行连接主机。价格已经上涨：二手V100 SXM2 32GB在eBay上目前约900美元一块，比帖子中约400美元一块翻了一倍多，而且挂牌价仍在上涨。系统其余配置包括Gigabyte Threadripper Pro主板、12核3945WX CPU、8条32GB DDR4 RDIMM、一个NUMA节点，以及总功率2800W的两个电源，分别接在普通办公电路上。这是二手数据中心硬件作为低成本、大容量快速VRAM方案的一个真实案例。

这套服务器目前每天用于案卷初筛：读取记录文件夹，提取事实、日期和数字，生成摘要，并对常规文书起草给出初稿。所有输出都要经过人工复核，这既是良好的“人在回路”策略，也能确保客户文件不被发送到云端或前沿模型。系统接入了RAG数据库和工具调用，操作者可通过SSH上的Discord风格界面从Windows PC驱动。目前它一次只处理一个请求。

模型方面，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash被压缩到以2比特为主，权重仍有248.8GB。模型中负责每个词大部分计算的“专家”部分完全驻留在GPU显存中，约110GB的查找表“Engram tables”则留在系统内存；从内存取数据每步约0.12毫秒，builder称几乎不影响速度。模型前半部分第0—19层跑在第一块SXM2基板上，后半部分第20—39层跑在第二块基板上。每块基板内部的重流量走自己的NVLink，因此每步只有一次交接需要跨过较慢的板间PCIe。此前builder发现，如果把每一层都拆分到八块卡上，速度会因为PCIe跳转而“断崖式下降”。

性能相当可观。代码生成最快可达215 tokens/s，因为DeepSeek内置的小型草稿模型会向前猜五个token，而代码容易猜中；法律写作最高118 tokens/s。长文档的启动较慢：模型读取提示词约2200 tokens/s，因此在128K tokens时首token约需一分钟；它最多可接受524K tokens上下文。三天前，同一模型在四块卡上只有36—38 tokens/s；加上第二块基板后性能跳升，理想情况下可能翻倍，builder将剩余提升归功于自定义kernel和prefill优化。按其测量，在1K、32K、128K、256K提示长度下，首token等待分别约1.2、17.2、59.2、118.7秒，代码吞吐为215、200、183、160 tokens/s，法律写作为118、117、111、103 tokens/s；测试采用贪心解码、输出1024 tokens、两次运行平均。

搭建并非即插即用。主机曾两次因连接某块GPU基板的PCIe链路发生致命错误而重启，两次都发生在提高功耗上限并解除GPU时钟限制时；此时显卡功耗达到192—232W，超过180W限制。builder猜测，但未证实，是负载尖峰时基板停止响应。在限制时钟并移除一块电源连接器有烧痕的基板后，重启停止；他提醒“检查你的连接器”。现在每块卡功耗上限设为150W，为其300W额定值的一半，图形时钟上限1522MHz；测试表明200W上限没有明显性能收益。系统内存还出现过不可纠正ECC错误，将RAM从DDR4-3200降到DDR4-2666后消失。上次检查时一块GPU以x4而非x8连接，builder计划重新插拔；有评论者称自己在V100上遇到同类问题，原因是坏线缆。

这套系统的价值在于：估计现有LLM工作流中有50%—60%可以在这台机器上运行，而不是调用前沿模型。另有一套由两台DGX Spark组成的第二DeepSeek服务器，两套系统会互相交接工作。相比API定价，这套方案看起来能省钱，但builder表示它并不真的更快；不过一旦实现自包含，就能保护客户数据，这是目标。V100机器还可能接入240V电路。除功耗外，系统还面临Nvidia R580驱动分支这一最后支持Volta的版本，未来支持时间有限。目前这主要是一项爱好，但未来可能成为商业想法；下一步是同时处理两到三个请求，相关功能已在测试系统上构建和检查，但尚未部署到服务器。

items.title: China builds massive 800-megawatt AI data center campus to rival US Stargate project
items.description: Envision has delivered the first 120MW of its Galaxy AI datacenter in less than a year, combining wind farms, battery storage and an unconventional cooling system to cut costs and keep power-hungry servers running
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China is building an 800MW AI data center campus in Inner Mongolia that could challenge the economics of America's Stargate project, according to a new report from SemiAnalysis. Envision has built the first 120 MW of Galaxy AI data center campus in less than a year, a cost the researchers put at just one-fifth of comparable US projects, after visiting the site in September.But getting the buildings up is only half of the battle. AI data centers need enormous amounts of electricity, and Envision is taking an unusual route to secure it— building its own wind farms and battery storage alongside the computing facility.While US developers are turning to on-site gas turbines to work around grid constraints, Envision is building its data center alongside wind farms, battery storage, and dedicated power infrastructure. Galaxy is located in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, and is being developed across four phases for two unnamed internet companies. The completed campus is planned to provide up to 800MW of IT capacity by the end of 2027, putting it closer to the approximately 820MW of critical IT capacity at the Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Envision is building its own power supply for Galaxy rather than leaving everything to the local grid. So far, the company has installed more than 100GW of wind turbines and wants its wind farms to provide over 60% of the electricity needed by the campus’s first two phases. Those farms, located about 80 kilometers apart, have a combined capacity of 420MW. That's well above the 240MW load expected from the first two phases, although wind turbines rarely get to run flat out. Ulanqab’s wind capacity factor is between 355 and 40%, so Envision is adding four-hour battery storage to keep the electricity coming when the wind dies down. (Image credit: SemiAnalysis)Power equipment is proving rather hard to come by for some US data center builders. We have previously reported on turbine shortages that have pushed delivery estimates to 2030, while SpaceX is looking to manufacture its own turbine blades for its gas-powered AI facilities. Envision, meanwhile, is putting wind generation and battery storage right alongside its servers. You may like China deploys 'world's first' 800-volt DC power system for massive AI data center China shifting massive AI data center complexes to rural provinces to tap surplus energy SpaceX's plan to build more data center compute than Google's entire lifetime capacity in just 1.5 years is possible, say analysts The power hardware inside the Galaxy is worth a look, too. Semianalyss visited a 5MW hall where solid-state transformers take 10kV AC electricity and convert it directly into 800V DC for the server racks. That's a fairly substantial departure from conventional data-center power distribution, which typically involves several intermediate conversion stages. “In one 5MW hall, we saw the 800V system at work,” the researchers wrote. They explained that “Solid-state transformers (SSTs) take 10kV AC from the grid and convert it straight to 800V DC for the racks.”The design removes several intermediate components found in conventional data center power systems, including low voltage transformers, uninterruptible power supplies and rectifiers. Fewer conversion stages can reduce equipment requirements and energy losses, although SemiAnalysis did not provide a measured efficiency improvement for Galaxy’s pilot. The 5MW installation is only a small part of the campus, but it puts the technology into operation at a live facility. Envision, however, plans an even larger deployment in the next construction phases, a move that aligns with Nvidia's push for 800V DC distribution in future high-density AI systems.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsGalaxy's campus uses a cooling arrangement in which liquid-cooled and air-cooled servers share a single water loop, eliminating the need for conventional central chiller plants. That matters as AI servers generate more heat and require increasingly sophisticated cooling systems. Removing central chillers can simplify infrastructure, although the design depends on local climate conditions and the facility's ability to reject heat through its water loop. China has previously experimented with other unconventional cooling methods, including a wind-powered underwater datacenter off Shanghai that uses surrounding seawater to help cool its servers.That said, Galaxy is the first major project in Invision's wider Inner Mongolia datacentre plans, which Semianalysis says add up to 3GW, with the rest of the campus still a busy construction site. The surrounding Chahar High-tech Zone is also expanding rapidly, with nearly 30,000 construction workers spread across 22 data center projects, according to a local report cited by the researchers.The wider Chinese expansion is also attracting some of the world's largest technology companies. Alibaba, Huawei and ByteDance are among the firms expanding infrastructure in the region, which benefits from relatively cheap electricity, available land and abundant wind resources. However access to electricity and datacenter buildings does not automatically translate to available AI computing power. China's access to advanced accelerators remains a separate constraint, particularly as US export restrictions limit its ability to acquire Nvidia’s most powerful chips. items.titleZh: 中国打造800兆瓦大型AI数据中心园区，对标美国“星际之门”项目
items.descriptionZh:
中国内蒙古正在建设一座规划IT容量最高达800MW的AI数据中心园区“Galaxy”，其开发方远景科技集团（Envision）计划以自建风电、储能和新型供电架构，挑战美国“Stargate”项目的经济性。SemiAnalysis在9月实地考察后发布的报告称，Galaxy首期120MW设施在不到一年内建成，建设成本仅为美国同类项目的约五分之一。项目位于乌兰察布，分四期开发，服务于两家未具名互联网公司，全部建成后计划到2027年底提供最高800MW IT容量，接近得克萨斯州阿比林Stargate园区约820MW的关键IT容量。这意味着中国在AI基础设施的规模、建设速度和成本控制上，正形成与美国超大规模AI数据中心相竞争的能力。

AI数据中心的核心瓶颈之一是电力。与部分美国开发商在电网约束下采用现场燃气轮机不同，远景选择为数据中心配套自建风电、电池储能和专用电力基础设施。报告称，远景迄今已在全球安装超过100GW风电机组；Galaxy前两期所需电力中，风电预计提供60%以上。为园区供能的风电场相距约80公里，合计容量420MW，高于前两期预计240MW负载。不过乌兰察布风电容量因子约为35%—40%，风机难以持续满发，因此项目配置了4小时电池储能，在风力下降时维持供电。这种“数据中心+新能源+储能”的模式，把发电资源与算力设施直接绑定，减少对当地电网的依赖，也利用内蒙古廉价电力、可用土地和丰富风资源。

在供电硬件上，Galaxy采用了不同于传统数据中心的架构。SemiAnalysis考察了一个5MW机房：固态变压器（SST）将电网10kV交流电直接转换为800V直流电，供服务器机架使用。传统数据中心通常需要多级转换，包括低压变压器、不间断电源（UPS）和整流器等；Galaxy的设计去除多项中间设备，理论上可减少设备需求和能量损耗，但报告未给出该试点机房实测效率提升数据。5MW系统目前只是园区一小部分，却已在真实设施中运行。远景计划在后续建设阶段扩大部署，这与Nvidia推动未来高密度AI系统采用800V直流配电的方向一致。

冷却方面，Galaxy让液冷服务器和风冷服务器共享同一水环路，取消传统中央冷水机组。随着AI服务器功率和发热量上升，冷却系统日益关键；去除中央冷机可简化基础设施，但该设计依赖当地气候条件以及设施通过水环路排热的能力。中国此前还探索过非常规冷却方式，例如上海附近利用海水冷却的风电水下数据中心。Galaxy是远景在内蒙古更大数据中心计划中的首个大型项目。SemiAnalysis称，远景在内蒙古的相关规划合计达3GW，园区其余部分仍是繁忙工地。周边察哈尔高新技术开发区也在快速扩张，当地报道称22个数据中心项目共有近3万名施工人员。

这一轮扩张吸引了阿里巴巴、华为、字节跳动等中国大型科技企业。该地区具备相对低廉的电价、可用土地和丰富风能资源。但报告也指出，获得电力和数据中心建筑并不自动等于拥有可用AI算力。中国获取先进加速器仍受独立约束，尤其是美国出口限制削弱其获得Nvidia最强芯片的能力。因此，Galaxy和内蒙古集群的意义不仅在于以新能源和新型直流供电降低AI数据中心成本、提升建设速度，也反映出在中美AI竞赛中，中国正试图以能源基础设施、建设效率和系统集成能力弥补高端芯片供应受限带来的短板。

items.titleZh: 现在以历史最低价399.99美元入手AMD最快的主流游戏CPU
items.descriptionZh:
AMD目前在游戏CPU市场占据主导地位。虽然Ryzen 7 9800X3D并非AMD产品线中绝对性能最强的型号，但凭借出色的性能功耗比，它仍被视为游戏玩家的最佳选择之一。当前该处理器在多家零售商处降至399.99美元的历史新低，不过需要应用优惠券：Newegg结账时使用优惠码BFF36可减70美元，Amazon则需点击价格下方49.01美元优惠券。

Ryzen 7 9800X3D采用AMD当前Zen 5架构，为8核16线程，加速频率5.2GHz，TDP 120W，并且完全解锁，可进行超频——这改善了AMD早期3D V-Cache芯片在超频方面的限制。其核心技术在于额外的大容量L3缓存：该芯片配备96MB L3缓存，并通过重新配置的芯片布局，将缓存堆叠在CPU核心下方、更靠近均热板的位置。这种设计使游戏性能显著受益，尤其适合对CPU敏感的负载。

性能对比方面，定位更高的Ryzen 7 9850X3D在1080p下仅比9800X3D快约3%，但功耗需求高出约30%。因此，9800X3D在每瓦性能上表现更优，可在不大幅增加功耗的情况下最大化游戏性能。基准测试显示，9800X3D处于CPU性能榜前列；搭配较新的显卡时瓶颈较少，若与RTX 5080或RTX 5090等高端GPU组合，可在各类游戏中实现高帧率。对于《赛博朋克2077》这类CPU密集型游戏，96MB L3缓存也能提供有力支持。

从市场影响看，Intel目前缺少能与之正面竞争的同类产品，因此9800X3D预计在较长时间内不会过时，并可能在未来数年继续主导游戏CPU市场。AMD的AM5平台仍在延续，AMD承诺至少再支持一代。对于现有AM5游戏PC升级或新装机用户，这两款X3D处理器都是颇具吸引力的核心选择。

此外，9850X3D也在促销：Newegg售价419美元，需使用优惠码BFF39减65美元；Amazon可通过页面优惠券获得同等价格。该型号同样基于Zen 5架构，8核16线程，加速频率5.6GHz，配备96MB 3D V-Cache。相比其484美元的发售价，当前419美元相当于明显降价。整体来看，9800X3D以399美元的历史低价提供极佳游戏性能功耗比，而9850X3D则以约3%的额外性能满足追求更高频率的用户。

history.title: Law firm files class-action lawsuit against Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang confirms affair with alleged Chinese spy
history.description: Class-action lawsuit and legal investigations against Nvidia over securities fraud start flying
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The baying of the hounds can be heard at a distance. Yesterday, Nvidia's Jensen Huang confirmed that it was indeed true that he had a romantic affair with Alice Huang (not related to the family), who U.S. intelligence services claim is a Chinese honeypot tasked with facilitating smuggling of the firm's advanced GPUs into China. Now, a class-action lawsuit and investigations have started flying from almost everywhere.This development is not unexpected, as basic securities law allows shareholders to sue their investees if they misrepresent facts or otherwise perform actions that cause a drop in stock prices. They may have a point, as Nvidia's shares dipped significantly when the confirmation of Jensen's infidelity and the ramifications thereof hit the press everywhere.The legal proceedings are bound to be numerous, but as of right now, the first class-action lawsuit was filed by the Rosen Law Firm. The suit claims that Nvidia and Jensen Huang failed to disclose or misled investors regarding Jensen's affair with Alice, lied about it when asked, raised national security concerns, and caused a subsequent loss of Nvidia's reputation. You can check out the case docket at PacerMonitor here.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While legal analysis is beyond the scope of this news, Nvidia did downplay Jensen's relationship with Alice, saying that "Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year."Other legal firms have launched their own investigations into the recent development, with essentially the same justification: Schall, Brown & Schwartz attributes a 5.5% pre-market-trading drop to Nvidia, as does Levi & Korsinsky. The office of Frank R. Cruz mentions an 8.8% figure related to intra-day exchanging, and is interested in shareholders with $50,000 in losses. The percentage-drop figure is 5.88% premarket for Bronstein, Gewritz & Grossman. You may like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to having an affair with suspected Chinese spy US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to Congress over affair with alleged Chinese spy Every investigation and suit mentioned here requires no upfront fees from complainants, as with most class-action lawsuits. The underlying condition is often that the law firms involved get a cut of whichever damages or settlements may appear at the end of the lawsuit. Some of them, like the one by Levi & Korsinsky, even aim to relieve investors who've already sold their Nvidia shares and sold them at a loss, with no minimum amount required.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors

history.titleZh: 律师事务所对英伟达提起集体诉讼，此前CEO黄仁勋承认与一名被指为中国间谍者发生婚外情
history.descriptionZh:
据该报道，英伟达CEO黄仁勋已确认与Alice Huang（报道称与黄家无亲属关系）存在婚外情；美国情报机构声称Alice Huang是中国“蜜罐”人员，任务是便利英伟达先进GPU走私进入中国。此事迅速引发集体诉讼和多起律所调查。报道指出，按照证券法基本规则，若公司或高管虚假陈述、误导投资者，或实施导致股价下跌的行为，股东可提起诉讼；黄仁勋相关确认及后续影响见诸媒体后，英伟达股价明显下跌，成为诉讼的重要背景。

首个集体诉讼由Rosen Law Firm提起。诉状称，英伟达和黄仁勋未披露或误导投资者关于黄仁勋与Alice关系的信息，在被询问时作出不实陈述，引发国家安全担忧，并导致英伟达声誉受损。英伟达则淡化黄仁勋与Alice的关系，称“Megaspeed与许多其他区域云客户并无不同；会见客户是CEO工作的一部分，黄仁勋每年与数千名客户高管交流”。

其他律所也宣布调查，理由类似：Schall, Brown & Schwartz和Levi & Korsinsky均提到英伟达盘前交易下跌5.5%；Frank R. Cruz办公室提到盘中交易相关跌幅8.8%，并关注损失达5万美元的股东；Bronstein, Gewritz & Grossman给出的盘前跌幅为5.88%。报道称，这些调查和诉讼通常不要求投诉人预付费用，律所往往从最终赔偿或和解中分成；Levi & Korsinsky还面向已亏损卖出英伟达股票的投资者，且无最低金额要求。原文未涉及GPU核心技术原理、创新点或性能参数对比，重点在于相关指控、法律诉讼及市场反应。

history.description:

history.content: It’s difficult to overstate Nvidia’s power in today’s AI landscape. The company’s chips are the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built, and demand has consistently outpaced supply for years. Nvidia has also been an influential investor in a wide range of up-and-coming AI companies in recent years, with about $99 billion worth of equity investments in frontier AI labs, neoclouds, infrastructure companies, and more. Its chief executive has even become close with President Donald Trump.This is why, as both cofounder and longtime CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang would be a valuable target for a foreign adversary with sights on the American AI industry.Huang is in hot water after news broke of his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) is an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider and a top Nvidia customer. Questions are swirling around how the affair may have influenced Huang’s reported push to sell advanced chips to China — and potentially even influenced President Trump’s own decisions surrounding AI export controls.Jensen Huang would be a valuable target for a foreign adversary with sights on the American AI industryUS officials believe the Megaspeed executive is a foreign intelligence asset that has funneled information straight to the Chinese government, per The New York Times — in particular, officials reportedly believe that Megaspeed is related to a convoluted web of Chinese companies working together to access chips in bulk and perhaps even illegally get some of those chips into China. Alibaba is reportedly one of Megaspeed’s top customers.“It’s not entirely surprising that the CEO of arguably one of the most important, if not the most important, AI chip companies is the target of some sort of intelligence-gathering from countries like China,” Hanna Dohmen, a senior research analyst at CSET, said in an interview with The Verge, adding that an alleged spy would potentially be interested in “better understanding what the US government is thinking on export controls,” as well as gathering information on Huang’s conversations with the Trump administration, attempting to influence policy, and gathering information on trade secrets like “who’s buying Nvidia’s chips, who’s getting them first, what’s coming next in terms of AI chips.”Megaspeed’s sister company, headquartered in Malaysia, spent $4.8 billion or more on Nvidia chips and technology between June 2024 and February 2026, the Times reported, citing trade records from trade platform ImportGenius. The transaction sizes were outside the norm for a small company, particularly when Nvidia chips are so difficult to get.”Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job”Nvidia spokespeople had said Huang’s relationship with the Megaspeed executive was strictly business. Their interactions were described as “not unusual or unexpected” in statements to the press. Nvidia’s line was, “Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job.”But at some point, their relationship became personal. In June 2024, just before Megaspeed became an Nvidia customer, photos show the two with other AI executives at a bar in Taipei after a local trade show; the following year, they reportedly had a business dinner in Taipei with others as well. But in private, according to US officials cited by the Times, the two’s relationship raised alarm bells for the US government — they had reportedly been surveilling the Megaspeed executive for months, if not longer, and that’s how it came out that she was in close contact with Huang.The revelation is particularly concerning because of Huang’s lobbying role. He’d been trying to convince the Trump administration and Congress to loosen export controls for sending advanced semiconductors to China, ostensibly so that Nvidia could sell more chips. We now know this was happening around the same time that Huang was spotted at the Taiwan dinner with Alice Huang in May 2025, according to Culper Research, which shorted Nvidia’s stock earlier this year. That dinner occurred shortly after Nvidia had shared the Trump administration’s new restrictions on its China-specific H20 chips in April.Just a couple months after the Taiwan dinner, Huang reportedly met with Trump in the Oval Office in July 2025 to plead his case for loosening export restrictions on Nvidia’s advanced semiconductors. Days later, the company announced that the administration had blessed sales of its H20 chips to China. Huang had argued that spreading American chips to China would help establish US technology as the standard, rather than allowing for Chinese chips to grow, according to The New York Times. After setbacks earlier in the second Trump term in export policy to China, Huang began speaking with then-White House AI czar David Sacks in 2025, who became the key advocate for Nvidia’s view that selling American chips to China would be beneficial, the Times reported.By October 2025, Huang was lobbying Trump to allow Nvidia to sell more advanced chips to China, ahead of Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, per the Times; but after Trump considered the proposal, he ultimately decided not to move forward. (That same month, Huang hired an external PR firm known for handling sex scandals, Wired reported.)Months later, in December 2025, Trump changed course slightly, allowing Nvidia to sell H20 chips to a greenlit list of “approved customers” in China, with the US government taking a 25 percent cut of those sales. The same rules would apply to other US chipmakers, he wrote on Truth Social at the time.“It is in Nvidia’s interest and in Jensen Huang’s interest to lobby for looser export control restrictions”CSET’s Dohmen said that during the past two years, the US has seen a light loosening of AI export control regulations under the Trump administration, driven partly by Huang’s own lobbying. But it’s important to note, she said, that “even without any kind of intelligence operations from the Chinese side, it is in Nvidia’s interest and in Jensen Huang’s interest to lobby for looser export control restrictions.” Any restrictions by definition stifle Nvidia’s business expansion and cut off potential sales to help it grow its already stunning market cap — which is currently about $4.25 trillion, second only to Apple.Huang’s relationship with Trump is also particularly relevant here. The president lavished praise on Huang during a speech last year, saying that until recently, he hadn’t even heard of Nvidia, and then he wanted to break it up. But after meeting Huang, he said, he understood why it would be difficult to re-create the company he’d built. More recently, Huang put Trump on speakerphone when the president called him during an appearance onstage at the All-In Summit, publicly displaying his close access to the Oval Office.This past spring, a classified memo — the writing of which was overseen by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, per the Times — circulated among Trump administration officials ahead of the president’s trip to China in May, warning of the Megaspeed executive’s alleged involvement in surveillance on behalf of China’s Ministry of State Security. Her reported goal was to learn about advanced AI chips in the US and try to influence them being made available to China on a large scale. Asked if he had known about the memo reviewed by Rubio at a press briefing on Monday, Trump said, “I’d certainly check with the intelligence people. It could have been mentioned. Certainly it didn’t make much of an impact on me.” Earlier in the briefing, he said he was unaware of the alleged spy connection ahead of his trip to China.Huang was initially left off the list of executives joining Trump on the trip, but the president later asked him to join. Trump had been briefed about a year ago that US intelligence believed the Megaspeed executive to be a China intelligence operative, according to the Times, and that she had a close relationship with a US citizen who turned out to be Nvidia’s CEO. At the time, he reportedly chose not to take action.So far, the allegations haven’t affected Huang’s future at Nvidia. He’ll continue to lead the company during the investigation. Trump has also stood by him since news broke of the affair, telling reporters this past weekend, “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it.”Nvidia said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised”On Sunday, Huang wrote an internal memo to Nvidia employees — some of which are his own family members — writing, “I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” He then addressed Nvidia’s board, partners, and shareholders, adding that he is “fully committed” to leading the company and “will work to earn back your confidence.” This weekend, Nvidia’s board of directors launched an independent investigation into the national security allegations. Huang will not have control over the participants in the investigation, and Nvidia said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”Morningstar senior equity analyst Brian Colello wrote in a note on Monday that Morningstar “can’t rule out the investigation fading away and Nvidia returning to business as usual,” particularly since Huang is the “only CEO the company has ever known.” There’s also the fact that Huang’s Nvidia struck deals in August with six large financial institutions to provide more than $500 billion in financing for the buildout of AI data centers and other infrastructure, and as the US-China AI race intensifies, those are high-stakes agreements.“It’s unclear to us what these partnerships and financing deals would look like with a different Nvidia CEO,” Colello wrote. “Costs of capital may rise for future investments if perhaps the most prominent CEO in the AI landscape is no longer orchestrating such deals.” Morningstar still maintained a very high uncertainty rating for the company, with Colello writing that it’s possible US approval of Nvidia to sell H20 chips to China will be revoked and that the company could ostensibly be sanctioned as well.Trump told reporters on Sunday that Huang should remain CEO of Nvidia and that he would “certainly take him” on his next trip to China. “I haven’t heard he’s done anything wrong,” Trump told reporters. “He dealt with somebody, but you know, so does everybody else.”

history.titleZh: 中国能从黄仁勋那里得到什么？
history.descriptionZh:
这则报道的核心并非英伟达发布了新的芯片架构或性能指标，而是围绕英伟达CEO黄仁勋的一起国家安全与出口管制风波：据《纽约时报》报道，黄仁勋被曝与据称是中国情报人员的Alice Huang（与黄仁勋无亲属关系）存在婚外情，而Alice Huang是新加坡云服务商Megaspeed的高管。Megaspeed是英伟达大客户，阿里巴巴据称也是其重要客户之一。美国官员认为，Alice Huang是外国情报资产，曾向中国政府传递信息；他们还怀疑Megaspeed与一个复杂的中国公司网络有关，该网络试图批量获取英伟达芯片，甚至可能将部分芯片非法运入中国。报道称，美国方面已对Alice Huang进行数月甚至更长时间的监视，并由此发现她与黄仁勋保持密切联系。

背景上，英伟达在当前美国AI产业中处于基础设施核心地位，其芯片供不应求，公司近年还向前沿AI实验室、新型云服务商（neocloud）、基础设施公司等投入约990亿美元股权。黄仁勋作为联合创始人和长期CEO，既是美国AI芯片产业的关键人物，也是出口管制政策的重要游说者。报道称，他一直在说服特朗普政府和国会放松对华先进半导体出口限制，理由是让美国芯片进入中国市场有助于确立美国技术标准，而不是让中国芯片生态成长。2025年4月，英伟达披露特朗普政府对其中国特供H20芯片实施新限制；同年5月，黄仁勋与Alice Huang等人被拍到在台北一场展会后出现在酒吧；2025年7月，黄仁勋据称在白宫椭圆形办公室会见特朗普，几天后英伟达宣布政府允许H20芯片对华销售。2025年10月，黄仁勋又在特朗普与中国国家主席习近平会晤前游说允许英伟达向中国销售更先进芯片，但特朗普最终未推进。2025年12月，特朗普政府转而允许英伟达向“获批客户”名单中的中国客户销售H20芯片，美国政府抽取25%销售分成，并表示类似规则适用于其他美国芯片制造商。报道还称，时任白宫AI事务负责人David Sacks成为英伟达“对华销售美国芯片有利”观点的重要倡导者。

技术上，原文没有披露新的芯片设计、制程或算力性能参数，因此不存在可直接对比的架构创新或跑分数据。可量化的是产业规模与交易规模：英伟达市值约4.25万亿美元，仅次于苹果；Megaspeed总部位于马来西亚的姐妹公司据贸易记录在2024年6月至2026年2月间花费48亿美元或更多购买英伟达芯片和技术，这一交易规模对一家小公司而言异常庞大，尤其考虑到英伟达芯片供应紧张。H20则是英伟达为遵守美国出口管制而面向中国市场设计的AI加速芯片，属于先进AI训练和推理基础设施的一部分；云服务商和neocloud可通过采购大量芯片提供AI算力，这也使其成为出口管制和供应链安全审查的敏感环节。报道所揭示的风险在于，若云服务商或关联公司成为芯片流向中国的渠道，美国出口管制的有效性、英伟达的合规义务以及美国AI芯片供应链安全都会受到冲击。

事件的政治与政策影响同样重大。2026年5月特朗普访华前，一份由国务卿鲁比奥监督撰写的机密备忘录在政府官员中流传，警告Alice Huang涉嫌为中国国家安全部从事监视活动，目标包括了解美国先进AI芯片并试图影响其大规模对华供应。特朗普在简报会上称，若被简报过“ certainly didn’t make much of an impact on me”，并称访华前不知道所谓间谍关联；黄仁勋最初不在随行企业高管名单中，后来被特朗普邀请加入。报道称，特朗普约一年前已听取简报，知道美国情报界认为Alice Huang是中国情报人员且与一名美国公民关系密切，该美国公民后来被确认是黄仁勋，但当时未采取行动。事件曝光后，黄仁勋向英伟达员工发内部备忘录，承认对妻子不忠并道歉，同时表示将“完全致力于”领导公司、努力赢回信任。英伟达董事会启动独立调查，黄仁勋不控制调查参与者；公司称“没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达商业秘密受到损害”。特朗普公开支持黄仁勋留任，称他“是个可敬的人”“没听说他做错什么”，并表示下次访华会带他同行。

市场与公司治理层面，Morningstar高级股票分析师Brian Colello认为，调查可能淡去、英伟达恢复常态，因为黄仁勋是公司“唯一已知的CEO”；但若换CEO，英伟达2025年8月与六家大型金融机构达成的、为AI数据中心等基础设施提供超过5000亿美元融资的协议可能面临更高资本成本。Morningstar仍维持对该公司很高的不确定性评级，并指出美国对英伟达H20对华销售的批准可能被撤销，公司甚至可能面临制裁。总体看，这起事件把AI芯片出口管制、云算力供应链、CEO游说、美国政治与国家安全调查交织在一起；其技术影响不在于某款芯片性能，而在于先进AI算力如何跨境流动、云服务商如何成为管制焦点，以及英伟达在中美AI竞赛中的政策风险与领导层稳定性。

history.content: President Trump held a White House press briefing earlier today and responded to several questions about his knowledge of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang said this weekend that he had been “​​unfaithful” to his wife, and the company has opened an investigation into Huang.Recent articles from The New York Times indicated that Trump had been aware of a relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, the suspected spy, before information about it became public. In October, The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed “roughly a year ago” on intelligence that Huang and the alleged spy, Alice Huang, had developed a close relationship, but he didn’t do anything with the information. Yesterday, the NYT reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio helped draft a memo to Trump officials about the relationship before Trump visited China in May.In the press conference, Trump wasn’t specific about when he learned of the affair. But Trump said Huang told him today that he had “no idea” the person was a spy.Here are Trump’s responses to questions about Jensen Huang from his press briefing today. You can watch a replay of the press conference on MS Now’s YouTube channel.When were you first informed that there was an issue with Jensen Huang and the affair? What was presented to you at the time?I would say that when I heard about it, first of all, I was amazed because I view him as a very high-quality person. I’ve known him a long time. It’s the largest, by value, the largest or one of the largest companies in the world. He did that with a chip. When you think about it, you’ve got a chip that’s 10 years advanced, can’t be… the Blackwell can’t even be copied. He’s an amazing guy.I just hope there’s no problem. If there is a problem, we’ll let you know about it. But I hope there’s no problem. I believe he’s suffering greatly. I read his statement. And I believe he’s suffering greatly. Moreso because of his family. His wife who he loves and his family. But he is definitely suffering.Just to follow up on the, “When were you first told of these potential issues with Mr. Huang?” You didn’t answer that question.Well I’ve been hearing about it, and I’ve been reading a little bit about it over a period of time. But, not too long ago.When is that?We’ll look into it. I know the FBI’s looking into it in terms of something else. I think that he’ll be in good shape.…Are you going to bring up the case of Jensen Huang with President Xi when you visit with him next week?No, I don’t think so. Maybe, I’m sure, President Xi will ask me about it. I just know Jensen very well. I just think he’s a very honorable man. He built a great company. American company. I think he’s a very honorable guy. I feel very confident that he’ll be in good shape.Sticking with Jensen Huang, when you went to China earlier this year in May, did you know about these alleged ties to the spy then?No, I didn’t hear about it then. But a lot of people have heard about it. And Jensen totally denies that. I asked him today, because I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling alright, how are you doing… and I asked him about that. He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy. I asked him that question, did you have any idea that she was a spy? He said, I had no idea that she was a spy. And I really believe him.…I want to put a finer point on when exactly you were made aware of the intelligence around Jensen Huang.Oh, I’d have to check. But this has been going on…But there are reports that Secretary Rubio put an intelligence memo out last year. Did you read that memo?I’d certainly check with the intelligence people. It could have been mentioned. Certainly it didn’t make much of an impact on me.

history.titleZh: 特朗普称他了解黄仁勋的这些情况
history.descriptionZh:
美国总统特朗普在白宫简报会上就英伟达CEO黄仁勋与疑似中国间谍Alice Huang的婚外情争议作出回应。事件背景是：黄仁勋周末承认对妻子“不忠”，英伟达已对黄仁勋展开调查；《纽约时报》此前报道称，特朗普大约一年前已听取相关情报简报，得知黄仁勋与Alice Huang关系密切，但未采取行动。昨日NYT又报道，美国国务卿鲁比奥在特朗普今年5月访华前，曾协助起草一份发给特朗普官员的备忘录，内容涉及这段关系。特朗普在简报会上没有明确说明自己首次得知此事的具体时间，只表示“不久前”听说过并读到一些信息，称需要核查；他还提到FBI正在调查“其他方面”的事项。

特朗普对黄仁勋个人评价很高，称其是“非常高质量的人”，长期相识，并称英伟达按市值计是全球最大或最大之一的企业，黄仁勋凭借芯片做到这一规模。他特别提到英伟达Blackwell芯片“领先10年”、无法被复制。这里需要说明，Blackwell是英伟达面向AI数据中心的新一代GPU架构平台，主要用于大模型训练、推理和高性能计算；但原文并未提供具体性能参数或对比数据，特朗普“领先10年、无法复制”的说法属于政治人物评价，不能视为可量化技术结论。其技术影响在于，Blackwell这类AI加速芯片是生成式AI基础设施的核心，广泛应用于云端AI训练推理、超算和数据中心，因而使英伟达处于中美科技竞争和出口管制的敏感位置。

特朗普表示，他今天与黄仁勋通话，询问其状况，并直接问对方是否知道该女子是间谍；黄仁勋称“完全不知道”，特朗普表示相信他。特朗普还说，黄仁勋正因家庭尤其妻子和家人而“非常痛苦”，希望此事没有问题，若有问题会对外说明。被问及下周与中国领导人会面是否会提及此案时，特朗普称不会主动提，但预计对方可能会问；他再次称黄仁勋“非常可敬”，相信其会“处于良好状态”。对于今年5月访华时是否已知情，特朗普称当时没听说；对于鲁比奥是否曾发情报备忘录，他说会向情报人员核实，备忘录“可能被提到过”，但对他“没有太大影响”。

总体看，这一新闻的核心不是芯片技术发布，而是AI芯片巨头高管安全审查、疑似间谍风险与中美科技博弈交织下的政治风波。特朗普的公开背书可能在短期内缓和黄仁勋面临的政治压力，但其得知情报的时间线、鲁比奥备忘录的处理以及英伟达内部调查，仍可能影响公司治理声誉和华盛顿对AI芯片供应链安全的审视。原文未给出Blackwell的具体规格和性能对比，因此摘要不宜补充量化参数。

history.titleZh: 迄今为止我们所知道的关于针对英伟达CEO黄仁勋的间谍丑闻的一切
history.descriptionZh:
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋近日承认与Megaspeed高管Alice Huang存在婚外情，事件已引发英伟达内部调查和全球舆论关注。相关报道还称，自去年以来，美国情报报告将Alice Huang（与黄仁勋无亲属关系）认定为一名中国国家安全部间谍；她同时是一家AI算力公司的高管，该公司通过租赁方式提供英伟达GPU访问能力。这一双重身份指控使事件从个人丑闻扩展至国家安全、出口管制和AI算力供应链安全议题。

背景上，英伟达近年来已成为特朗普政府推动AI战略的关键企业，也是围绕中国能否获得尖端AI硬件谈判中的核心角色。凭借超过4万亿美元市值，英伟达还通过投资等方式支持其他AI公司，其中包括CoreWeave等“neoclouds”。这类新兴云服务商以GPU云租赁为核心商业模式，客户无需自建数据中心即可租用英伟达GPU算力，用于大模型训练、推理和其他AI工作负载。由于先进GPU是AI训练的关键基础设施，且受美国对华出口管制约束，任何涉及GPU租赁、转售或跨境访问的渠道都可能成为监管和情报关注重点。

技术上，新闻本身并未披露新的芯片架构或性能参数，核心在于AI算力供给模式：GPU云租赁将昂贵且供应紧张的加速卡资源池化，通过云服务向多家客户提供访问权限。这种模式提高了算力利用效率、降低了AI企业准入门槛，但也扩大了先进芯片流向敏感对象的潜在风险，使算力服务商成为出口管制和国家安全审查的关键节点。所谓“neocloud”正是围绕GPU租赁形成的新型云基础设施业态，CoreWeave等公司是英伟达的重要客户和生态伙伴。

目前，英伟达和黄仁勋表示“没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达机密受到损害”，但这一表态尚未平息外界质疑，调查仍在继续。事件可能影响英伟达与美国政府的关系、AI算力租赁行业的合规审查，以及围绕对华AI硬件出口的政策讨论。应用层面，该事件凸显GPU云算力在AI训练推理、数据中心和创业公司中的基础性作用，也表明AI芯片供应链安全已不仅是技术问题，而是商业、监管与地缘政治交织的敏感领域。

history.content: After publishing a support article in early September outlining usage limits for some Apple Intelligence features, the company has updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for a one-time purchase price of $49.99, as spotted by 9to5Mac. It has a built-in AI assistant to do things like “start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project.”These Intelligence Usage Packs, as Apple calls them, will allow users to continue accessing certain Apple Intelligence features that have usage limits because they rely on cloud-based AI models from OpenAI or Google Gemini. The Usage Packs can only be used by the Apple Account that purchased them (Family Sharing isn’t supported) and, as Apple explains on its website, any unused additional usage will roll over from month to month, but will expire 12 months after it was purchased.For Logic Pro, Apple says the usage limit is “impacted by the complexity of conversations you have with the assistant.” Users finding themselves running out of access can find the option to buy an Intelligence Usage Pack in the Intelligence Features > Show Usage section of the app’s main menu. Currently, only Logic Pro has the option to buy more usage, but it’s expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers that are getting access to Apple’s AI chatbot.

苹果在9月初发布支持文档，说明部分Apple Intelligence功能存在使用限制。随后，公司更新了音乐制作软件Logic Pro，新增“Buy More Usage（购买更多使用量）”选项，用户可通过一次性支付49.99美元购买Intelligence Usage Pack。Logic Pro内置AI助手，可执行“开始一首新歌、通过单条提示设置人声轨道，或优化当前项目”等任务。此次变化意味着，依赖云端AI模型的Apple Intelligence功能开始以“使用包”形式提供配额补充。

从技术机制看，Apple Intelligence的部分功能并非完全在端侧运行，而是调用OpenAI或Google Gemini等云端AI模型，因此存在使用配额。苹果将这些补充配额称为Intelligence Usage Packs，用于让用户在达到限制后继续访问相关功能。使用包只能由购买它的Apple Account使用，不支持家庭共享；未使用的额外用量可逐月结转，但会在购买12个月后过期。苹果表示，Logic Pro的使用限制“受用户与助手对话复杂程度影响”，但未披露具体次数或token额度。用户可在应用主菜单的“Intelligence Features > Show Usage”中找到购买入口。

目前只有Logic Pro提供购买更多使用量的选项，但苹果预计本月将把该机制扩展到其他Apple Creator Studio应用，包括Pixelmator Pro、Final Cut Pro、Motion，以及将获得苹果AI聊天机器人访问权限的Pages、Keynote和Numbers。此举反映出专业创作软件中的云端AI功能正从统一包含转向按需购买配额，既有助于苹果转嫁云端推理成本，也可能影响专业用户对AI助手使用成本和使用规划的预期。由于尚未公布具体配额单位和消耗规则，用户实际使用成本仍取决于对话复杂度和功能调用频率。

history.content: Anthropic is announcing two new models today: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says are designed to take on “daunting” technical challenges. The company claims the new models show improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, and can generate outputs faster than the 5.1 versions of the Fable and Mythos models.Claude Fable 5.2 is good at challenging software engineering problems, Anthropic says, and can orchestrate agent teams and tackle long-running projects. The new model has also solved some complex scientific problems, including two open theoretical physics problems.During prerelease testing, the two models have “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours,” Anthropic says.Claude Fable 5.2 is launching today. As for Claude Mythos 5.2, only vetted organizations will have access to start. The new 5.2 models follow the release of Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 in September.

history.descriptionZh:
Anthropic 今日发布 Claude Fable 5.2 与 Claude Mythos 5.2，定位是应对“艰巨”技术挑战，接续今年9月推出的 Claude Fable 5.1 和 Claude Mythos 5.1。官方称，5.2 版本在编码、推理和视觉能力上较 5.1 有所提升，输出速度也更快；但新闻稿未披露模型架构、训练方法、参数量或具体基准分数，因此目前可确认的主要是能力定位和预发布测试案例，而非底层技术原理细节。

Fable 5.2 被描述为擅长高难度软件工程问题，能够编排智能体团队并处理长周期项目。Anthropic 称，在预发布测试中，两款模型帮助工程师完成原本难以实施的软件迁移，从零设计出三个可工作的电子设备，解决黑洞物理中的两个开放问题，在机器人评测上取得实质进展，并在30小时内形式化费马大定理的证明。这些案例覆盖软件工程、硬件设计、物理与数学科研、机器人评估等场景，显示模型能力正从单点问答向长流程、多步骤技术任务扩展。相较5.1，官方强调其在编码、推理、视觉和输出速度上的提升，但未给出可横向比较的量化性能表。

发布节奏上，Fable 5.2 今日推出；Mythos 5.2 初期仅向经过审核的组织开放。其潜在应用包括企业软件迁移与现代化、复杂项目自动化、智能体协同、科研问题探索、电子设备原型设计、机器人评测以及数学形式化等。Mythos 5.2 的受限访问也表明，Anthropic 对高能力模型采取审慎部署策略。

history.title: Nvidia cracks down on overseas cloud AI GPU rentals for China
history.description: Nvidia may cap cloud partners’ Chinese business at 49% as Chinese firms buy up more than 1 million gaming and workstation GPUs.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia-based compute is getting scarce and expensive for Chinese AI labs on both of their main routes, buying export-compliant cards and renting abroad, and the Financial Times reports that Nvidia’s own crackdowns are part of the reason. Nvidia has told cloud partners worldwide that at least 51% of their services must go to non-Chinese firms, while Chinese companies have bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation cards this year to cover the shortfall. Meanwhile, a B300 rack that sells for about $600,000 internationally reportedly fetched $2.8 million in China last month.Chinese customers have ordered more than 6 million of Nvidia’s export-compliant RTX Pro 5500 cards. That is at least twice the 3 million that the company could reportedly manufacture in 2027. One source told CNBC that it was proposed that Moonshot pay 30% to 50% more upfront, in comparison to a non-Chinese entity.Many Chinese groups have relied on overseas leases for advanced AI work, which can include model training, and these tech groups have been the biggest clients for data centers in Southeast Asia. Data centers unable to find non-Chinese clients could be forced to pull back supply, and it’s “difficult to find enough non-Chinese clients outside the US,” one Singapore-based group told the FT. While Nvidia hasn’t confirmed or denied its new rule, implementing it would ease criticism from U.S. lawmakers just as Chinese demand is growing.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: What Nvidia told partners has come through verbal instructions, via sales and regional teams, and applies globally rather than just in Asia. Existing deals and leases are not changed, but new ones must comply. Nvidia’s whitelist more than halved its authorized Asian buyer count, which encouraged more Chinese groups to lease over other options, including smuggling. On top of this, Fleet Intelligence tracking is now required for Southeast Asian providers that want to become Nvidia Cloud Partners. All of these combined — whitelist, cap, and tracking — may act to alleviate U.S. concerns.Among companies that have moved to renting, Moonshot has held discussions to rent capacity from neoclouds that host in Europe with Nvidia GPUs. Specifically, it’s looking for Nvidia Blackwell systems, which export controls bar from China; one source said the talks covered clusters of 8,000 or more Blackwell GPUs in Europe. These clusters would handle inference, serving models to end users, and the European talks for them happened after the White House said Moonshot accessed Blackwell chips through a facility in Thailand. The firm has been fervent about its intentions to secure more compute. You may like Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia GPUs in a single year, report claims China’s tech giants drop $35 billion on export-compliant Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 workstation GPU orders to power AI ambitions, according to reports Nvidia tells data center operators to limit business from Chinese customers with new global restrictions, report claims Moonshot isn't the only Chinese company looking to secure Nvidia chips for AI training. Tencent has a deal with Oracle to lease 100,000 GPUs in Southeast Asian data centers. ByteDance and Alibaba are also pursuing similar long-term leases, and most of these overseas data centers run chips like the forbidden B300. MiniMax, like Moonshot, also leases significant compute both at home and abroad.The big reason is that domestic AI chip supply is simply not up to the task, although not for a lack of trying. Huawei is expected to hit 1.6 million chips this year, with about 1 million from Alibaba and Baidu, and 300,000 from Cambricon. Total supply this year will be up to 3.5 million, including about 1 million made overseas, against a demand that far exceeds 5 million. That number could more than double next year.Part of the problem is that the export-compliant cards Chinese firms have been buying, mostly the RTX Pro 6000D, RTX Pro 5000, and RTX 5090, are mostly useful for simpler work such as prefill. Even so, the discontinued 6000D’s pricing in China has reportedly doubled. Huawei’s Ascend 910C outperforms them in most areas, but these lower-end options are still coveted, partly because of a preference for CUDA over Huawei’s CANN. Nvidia’s programming platform is supported by most AI frameworks and libraries, and much in-house code is optimized for it.Then there’s the RTX Pro 5500, with 84GB of GDDR7 with ECC and 1,398 GB/s of memory bandwidth. The card runs on a full PCIe Gen 5 x16 interface, draws up to 600 W, and can be split into up to two MIG instances. That still leaves it well short of a B300, which has about 3.4 times the memory and 5.7 times the bandwidth, plus NVLink, which the 5500 lacks. Swipe to scroll horizontally What Chinese labs can buy vs. what they rent GPU Memory Bandwidth Interconnect Status for Chinese buyers RTX Pro 5500 84GB GDDR7 1.4 TB/s PCIe Gen 5 x16 Export-compliant; samples in December, deliveries from Q1 2027 H200 141GB HBM3E 4.8 TB/s NVLink Licensed by the U.S. case by case; Beijing withholding approval for large-scale imports B300 288GB HBM3E 8 TB/s NVLink (1.8 TB/s) Banned for sale to China; rented abroad Indicated orders from China are not precise, but the total of over six million includes more than three million from ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent. The big three ordered at about $11,400 each, for a total sticker price over $35 billion. This is difficult to fill when there may be fewer than three million produced next year, and partners might only actually get 5% to 10% of the original ask. Starting in 2027, much of Nvidia’s TSMC capacity may shift to Rubin, taking more production, while the RTX Pro 5500’s early samples are due in December. What to read next Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network H200s finally reach China under case-by-case import licenses, but it's already too late for Nvidia Chinese AI lab Moonshot reportedly looked at European data centers to access Nvidia chips, report claims On the legal side, it’s currently easier to rent than to own as current U.S. law does not give regulators broad authority over overseas cloud access. The Remote Access Security Act (RASA), which would extend U.S. export controls to that area, has sailed through the House but has not yet passed the Senate. Those directly affected — neoclouds and related financiers — price in a possible ban regardless, which drives the upfront premium.China’s side is not completely clean, either, with about 600,000 H200s reportedly stuck in storage in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to the mainland. Beijing is withholding approvals for large-volume imports such as this. Only relatively small quantities have come in during recent months, for some big internet companies, with others coming through intermediaries and indirect routes in small quantities. The price: over $900,000 for an eight-card H200 server in China at the end of last month, about 3x the cost a year ago. This is despite the fact that H200 sales are already under U.S. license.The first test that will show how many cards will actually land occurs in Q1 2027, when the RTX Pro 5500 is expected in commercial deliveries. For rentals, whether or not the Remote Access Security Act is a factor depends on a Senate vote, which is not yet scheduled. Nvidia’s Q3 results come in soon, on Nov. 17, which could bring some illumination.With CEO Jensen Huang under scrutiny lately over reports that he was targeted by an alleged Chinese spy, which Nvidia’s board is now investigating, he’s going to feel the heat even more just a day later, when lawmakers have asked him to attend a closed-door briefing. He’s been pushing for laxer controls and more access, so the assumed 51% rule will also be put to the test.
history.author: Shane Downing
history.titleZh: 英伟达严打海外云AI GPU对华租赁
history.descriptionZh:
英伟达算力对中国AI实验室正变得越来越稀缺和昂贵。中国AI企业获取先进算力的两条主要路径——购买出口合规芯片和赴海外租用数据中心——都受到挤压。据《金融时报》报道，英伟达自身收紧渠道管控是原因之一。英伟达已通过销售和区域团队以口头方式告知全球云合作伙伴，其服务中至少51%必须提供给非中国公司，且这一要求适用于全球而非仅亚洲；现有交易和租约不受影响，但新交易必须遵守。英伟达尚未确认或否认该规则，但若实施，可能在美国 lawmakers 批评中国需求增长之际缓解压力。

供应端缺口显著。中国公司今年已购买超过100万颗英伟达游戏和工作站显卡以弥补算力不足；中国客户还订购了超过600万颗出口合规的RTX Pro 5500，至少是英伟达2027年据称300万颗产能的两倍。价格也水涨船高：国际市场售价约60万美元的B300机架，上个月在中国据报被炒到280万美元。有消息称，有提议要求Moonshot比非中国实体多预付30%至50%的费用。英伟达的白名单已将其授权亚洲买家数量削减一半以上，促使更多中国集团转向租赁而非其他选项，包括走私；东南亚提供商若想成为英伟达云合作伙伴，还需接受Fleet Intelligence追踪。白名单、51%上限和追踪机制叠加，可能缓解美国监管担忧。

海外租赁成为中国企业获取高端算力的重要替代。许多中国集团依赖海外租约开展先进AI工作，包括模型训练，并成为东南亚数据中心的最大客户。无法找到非中国客户的数据中心可能被迫减少供应，而一家新加坡公司对《金融时报》表示，在美国以外“很难找到足够的非中国客户”。Moonshot已讨论从在欧洲托管英伟达GPU的neoclouds租用算力，具体寻找出口管制禁止对华销售的英伟达Blackwell系统；消息称谈判涉及欧洲8000颗以上Blackwell GPU的集群，用于推理和向终端用户提供模型服务。这些欧洲谈判发生在白宫称Moonshot通过泰国设施获取Blackwell芯片之后。腾讯则与Oracle达成协议，在东南亚数据中心租用10万颗GPU；字节跳动和阿里巴巴也在寻求类似长期租约，且多数海外数据中心运行B300等被禁止对华销售的芯片。MiniMax同样在国内外租赁大量算力。

根本原因是国内AI芯片供应仍不足以满足需求。华为今年预计出货160万颗，阿里巴巴和百度合计约100万颗，寒武纪约30万颗；今年中国AI芯片总供应预计最高350万颗，其中包括约100万颗海外制造，而需求远超500万颗，明年可能翻倍以上。中国公司购买的合规卡主要是RTX Pro 6000D、RTX Pro 5000和RTX 5090，更多适用于预填充等较简单工作；即便如此，已停产的6000D在中国价格据报翻倍。华为昇腾910C在多数领域优于这些低端合规卡，但后者仍受青睐，部分原因是开发者更偏好英伟达CUDA生态而非华为CANN——多数AI框架和库支持CUDA，大量内部代码也针对其优化。

从参数看，RTX Pro 5500配备84GB GDDR7 ECC显存，内存带宽1398GB/s，采用完整PCIe Gen 5 x16接口，功耗最高600W，可拆分为最多两个MIG实例。但它仍远不及B300：后者约有3.4倍显存和5.7倍带宽，并具备NVLink，而RTX Pro 5500没有。对比表显示，RTX Pro 5500为84GB GDDR7、1.4TB/s带宽、PCIe Gen 5 x16，属于出口合规产品，12月提供样品、2027年一季度开始交付；H200为141GB HBM3E、4.8TB/s带宽、NVLink，美国逐案许可，但北京对大规模进口暂不批准；B300为288GB HBM3E、8TB/s带宽、NVLink 1.8TB/s，禁止对华销售，只能海外租用。

中国指示性订单并不精确，但超过600万颗的总量中，字节跳动、阿里巴巴和腾讯合计超过300万颗。三大巨头订购单价约1.14万美元，总标价超过350亿美元；由于明年产量可能不到300万颗，这一订单难以满足，合作伙伴实际可能只拿到原始请求的5%至10%。从2027年起，英伟达很大一部分台积电产能可能转向Rubin，进一步占用生产资源；RTX Pro 5500早期样品预计12月出现。法律层面，目前租赁比拥有更容易，因为现行美国法律未赋予监管机构广泛的海外云访问管辖权。《远程访问安全法案》（RASA）拟将美国出口管制扩展至该领域，已通过众议院但尚未通过参议院。受影响的neoclouds及相关融资方已提前计入可能的禁令风险，从而推高预付溢价。中国方面也并非完全畅通：约60万颗H200据报滞留在香港等待运往内地，北京扣留大规模进口批准，近月只有相对小量进入一些大型互联网公司，其他通过中间商和间接渠道小批量流入。上月底，中国八卡H200服务器价格超过90万美元，约为一年前的3倍，尽管H200销售已处于美国许可之下。

第一个检验实际有多少芯片能落地的节点是2027年一季度，届时RTX Pro 5500预计开始商业交付。租赁路径是否受RASA影响，取决于尚未排期的参议院投票。英伟达第三季度财报将于11月17日发布，可能提供更多线索。与此同时，CEO黄仁勋近期因有报道称其被 alleged 中国间谍针对而受到审视，英伟达董事会正在调查；仅一天后，lawmakers 又要求他参加闭门简报，压力进一步上升。黄仁勋一直推动放松管制和扩大市场准入，因此所谓51%规则也将面临检验。

history.content: I would prefer that these people’s sex lives were none of my business but I guess we have to talk about Jensen Huang and the National Security Incident. Who could have guessed that the guy who was out here signing titties might not have great judgment about how to behave around women?Alice Huang — no relation to Jensen — is a former TV reporter. That was before she became “an executive” at Megaspeed, which bought $4.8 billion of hard-to-get Nvidia chips, starting around the time she was being photographed with Jensen in a Taipei bar in 2024. “To many in the industry, the well-funded push by Megaspeed into A.I. appeared to come out of nowhere,” The New York Times wrote, tactfully. Our girl Alice is also an alleged honeypot who was recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security. (China is denying all this, btw.)You know shit is going good when your corporate spokesperson has to tell the Times that of course your company does not disclose classified information to your customersWhat is Megaspeed? Well. The company has ties to the Chinese military and builds data centers in “Southeast Asia” (it has offices in Singapore and Indonesia) to sell compute to Alibaba. The chips it is using to do that are banned from being imported to China. Incidentally, Nvidia has been lobbying very intensely to get rid of import controls on its chips so it can sell them in China.This is all public knowledge in part because Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly “oversaw” a memo detailing Alice’s recruitment and relationship with Jensen, and then someone leaked it. (Powerful memo game, Marco, getting credit for one you didn’t even write!) Rubio passed his little note around in May, ahead of a trip to China taken by President Donald Trump. Jensen initially didn’t make the list of invitees on the trip — at least, not until Trump saw media coverage of the perceived snub. Trump and Jensen? They’re close. Which makes it even more interesting that Trump was personally briefed on the findings and did nothing, according to the Times.You know shit is going good when your corporate spokesperson has to tell the Times that of course your company does not disclose classified information to your customers. John Rizzo, the spokesman, also told the Times that Nvidia’s customers don’t ask Nvidia to lobby for changes to the chip restriction. Bit of a hat on a hat, John. First of all, they don’t have to — Nvidia’s financial incentives do it for them. Second, imagine this is a regular company. The business model of Megaspeed is that the chips are restricted, and that Megaspeed gets ahold of them. Megaspeed has no incentive to upend this situation! Unless, you know, it’s acting against its financial interest because it’s a front for Chinese spies… in which case, that statement is going to be embarrassing.Speaking of embarrassing, Rizzo told the Times “that Mr. Huang’s interactions with Ms. Huang were ‘not unusual’ and consistent with the kinds of meetings he has with any of Nvidia’s many customers.” Oh, okay. Who else was Jensen fucking?Nvidia has an extraordinary structureBecause two days after that statement, Jensen sent the most incredible email addressed “To my colleagues at Nvidia” in which he admitted he had been “unfaithful.” Then, he wrote, “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.” Are… your wife and family on the Nvidia employee email list?Well, yes! His son is a director of product management; his daughter is a senior marketing director. He even gave a job to his son-in-law!Also, Nvidia has an extraordinary structure. Jensen has 60 direct reports. Leave aside that there is no possible way to manage that many people well. I would like to direct your attention to something else entirely: If he is in trouble, there is no part of the company that is untouched. The usual problems attain, of course — he was in a position to have gotten any information she might have requested! He could have left company laptops available for infiltration! But because of the structure, he also could have issued commands to his many direct reports that benefited the CCP. Neat! I sure hope someone who knows a lot about cybersecurity is going through Nvidia with a fine-toothed comb.Is he in trouble? Well, Nvidia is opening an investigation into Jensen, who is also its largest individual shareholder. (At least there’s no dual-class stock!) Nvidia shares are, as of this writing, down almost five percent, which seems like an underreaction.I don’t know where Jensen’s actual wife, Lori, is in all thisPerhaps more consequentially, the Democratic Party just swept back into power and Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) seems mad. Also, the voters hate the data centers that house Nvidia chips, and I notice a lot of ambitious politicians thinking about the next presidential elections. For instance, there’s Rubio’s name attached to the memo. I also notice Trump’s popularity is at an all-time nadir. Besides any Democrats positioning themselves for a run, a Republican looking to create some daylight between himself and Trump could easily do so by going to town on Jensen, who is Trump’s buddy. I do not think Rubio is the only ambition monster to worry about.I don’t know where Jensen’s actual wife, Lori, is in all this. They got married in 1985. She gave up her job as a microchip designer to raise their kids. I would be very surprised if there is a prenup. I would be somewhat surprised if there was a postnup. Jensen doesn’t own as much of Nvidia as Jeff Bezos did of Amazon when he cheated on and divorced his wife, but it’s something to keep an eye on, if Lori decides she’s out.We’ve talked once or twice about Nvidia’s central role in the AI ecosystem — and specifically, that it is heavily involved in financing AI neoclouds. It has investments in SpaceX, CoreWeave (where it was, as of the time of the IPO, the company’s second-biggest customer), and OpenAI, among others. Jensen has been promoting “compute as an asset class.”Nvidia is, effectively, the central bank of AIOne of the reasons I have been uncertain about when and how the AI bubble will pop is that it seems to me that Nvidia can bail out any or all of these companies anytime it needs to, just like it did for CoreWeave when its IPO was threatened. Neoclouds exist because Nvidia wanted to create competition for its chips, so its biggest customers — Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle — couldn’t exert too much pricing pressure. Certainly I am not the only person who has noticed that Nvidia is, effectively, the central bank of AI. If Nvidia is in a particularly bad way, it kind of seems like, at minimum, the neoclouds get fucked too. Oddly, CoreWeave is up about 6 percent as of this writing; the stock market moves in mysterious ways.Maybe that is why our nation’s foremost thought leaders on X are posting things like “Whomst among us hasn’t accidentally fucked a Chinese spy? That’s how it is on this bitch of an earth.” I’m kidding, here’s investor/loudmouth Bill Ackman: “We should all support him and his family. Onward.” Shaun Maguire, partner at VC firm Sequoia: “I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.” (Elon Musk took a quick break from complaining about Dave Chappelle’s comedy to type “I agree” to Maguire’s note.)So Jensen can’t go down, as there’s no one who can replace him, and Nvidia can’t go down, as nothing can replace it. The AI industry better hope there isn’t some further revelation coming that would make one of these things unavoidable, such as the investigation finding proof that Alice directly accessed Nvidia’s systems while Jensen was showering or something. Might also be bad if, say, a US Commerce Department inquiry into Megaspeed was halted after Nvidia intervened. Didn’t we just hear somewhere that Jensen had been influencing the Trump administration’s policy on export controls?Anyway, as of this note, Jensen isn’t planning to step down as CEO. Might as well settle in for the most fun we’ll have until we find out that Musk did IVF with a family member of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

history.titleZh: AI的未来取决于……黄仁勋的性生活？
history.descriptionZh:
据《纽约时报》报道，英伟达CEO黄仁勋与Megaspeed高管Alice Huang的私人关系及后者涉嫌中国国家安全部“蜜罐”招募，正演变为涉及美国对华AI芯片出口管制、英伟达公司治理和AI算力生态的系统性事件。Alice Huang与黄仁勋无亲属关系，曾是电视记者，后成为Megaspeed“高管”。Megaspeed自2024年前后购入价值48亿美元、当时难以获得的英伟达芯片；《纽约时报》谨慎地称，在业内许多人看来，Megaspeed资金充裕的AI进军“像是凭空出现”。报道还称，Alice Huang被指由中国国家安全部招募为“蜜罐”，中方否认相关指控。Megaspeed被指与中国军方有联系，在新加坡和印尼设有办公室，并在东南亚建设数据中心，向阿里巴巴出售算力，而其使用的芯片被禁止进口至中国。与此同时，英伟达一直在大力游说放松对华芯片出口限制，以扩大在华销售。

从技术与商业模式看，本文不涉及新芯片架构或性能参数突破，核心争议在于受出口管制的AI加速芯片如何通过境外数据中心向中国客户提供算力，以及英伟达主导的“neocloud”融资模式。所谓neocloud，是专门提供AI算力的新兴云服务商；报道称，英伟达投资了SpaceX、CoreWeave和OpenAI等，其中CoreWeave在IPO时是英伟达第二大客户。英伟达扶持neocloud，部分目的是为其芯片制造竞争，避免微软、亚马逊、谷歌、甲骨文等大客户形成过强定价压力。黄仁勋还推销“算力作为资产类别”的概念。报道认为，英伟达实际上已成为“AI的中央银行”，可在必要时救助这些公司，就像CoreWeave IPO受威胁时那样；若英伟达自身陷入严重困境，neocloud也会受重创。截至报道时，英伟达股价跌近5%，CoreWeave则涨约6%。

事件的政治与安全背景包括：美国国务卿鲁比奥据报“监督”了一份详细描述Alice Huang被招募及其与黄仁勋关系的备忘录，该备忘录于5月传阅，随后泄露；特朗普总统访华前，黄仁勋最初不在邀请名单上，直到特朗普看到媒体关于其被冷落的报道后才被加入。报道称，特朗普与黄仁勋关系密切，且特朗普本人听取了相关调查简报但未采取行动。英伟达发言人John Rizzo对《纽约时报》称，公司当然不会向客户披露机密信息，客户也没有要求英伟达游说改变芯片限制；他还称黄仁勋与Alice Huang的互动“并非不寻常”，符合黄与众多客户会面的情形。但报道指出，英伟达自身财务激励已足以推动游说，而Megaspeed的商业模式恰恰依赖芯片限制存在，因此除非其作为中国间谍前台行动，否则没有财务动机颠覆这一局面。

公司治理层面，黄仁勋在Rizzo表态两天后向“英伟达同事们”发送全员邮件，承认自己“不忠”，并向妻儿道歉。报道称，黄仁勋的儿子是产品管理总监，女儿是高级营销总监，女婿也获得职位；黄仁勋有60名直接汇报对象，这种结构意味着若他出现问题，公司几乎没有部门不受影响：他可能接触敏感信息、使公司笔记本电脑暴露于渗透风险，也可能通过众多直接汇报者下达有利于中方的指令。英伟达已对黄仁勋展开调查，黄是公司最大个人股东；报道称至少公司没有双重股权结构。黄仁勋的妻子Lori于1985年结婚，曾为微芯片设计师，后放弃工作育儿；报道认为若离婚，可能影响黄仁勋的持股。政治层面，民主党重新掌权后，参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦似乎对此不满；选民对承载英伟达芯片的数据中心存在反感；鲁比奥的名字附在备忘录上；特朗普支持率处于低点，共和党人若想与特朗普保持距离，也可能借攻击黄仁勋获利。

支持者方面，投资人Bill Ackman呼吁支持黄仁勋及其家庭；红杉资本合伙人Shaun Maguire称黄仁勋对美国AI领导地位“不可替代”，马斯克表示同意。报道的结论是：黄仁勋不能倒，因为无人可替代；英伟达不能倒，因为无可替代。AI行业只能希望不会出现进一步爆料，例如调查发现Alice Huang直接访问英伟达系统，或美国商务部对Megaspeed的调查因英伟达干预而停止——而此前已有黄仁勋影响特朗普政府出口管制政策的讨论。截至该报道，黄仁勋不计划辞任CEO。整体看，事件凸显AI芯片供应链的地缘政治风险、关键人物与公司治理风险，以及英伟达在AI算力生态中的系统重要性。

history.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to Congress over affair with alleged Chinese spy
history.description: Jensen Huang has been summoned to appear before Congress's Select Committee on the CCP.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 12 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Less than 24 hours after he admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese spy, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been asked to appear before the House Select Committee on China. The Committee issued a letter today, signed by Rep. Brian J. Mast (R-FL), Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI), and Rep. Eric A. Crawford (R-AK). An X post featuring the letter states that the letter "expresses concerns over NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and Mr. Huang’s reported ties to a Chinese intelligence-linked executive of a Singapore-based data center company."ICYMI: Chairman @RepMoolenaar, Chairman @RepBrianMast, and Chairman @RepRickCrawford have sent a letter to NVIDIA CEO @JensenHuang asking him to appear before their three committees this month. The letter expresses concerns over NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and Mr. Huang’s reported ties to a Chinese intelligence-linked executive of a Singapore-based data center company.November 9, 2026"Dear Mr. Huang: We are writing to request that you appear before our committees for a joint, closed-door briefing on NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang," the letter begins.It goes on to say that recent reports surrounding the affair "raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information. "The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The closed-door hearing is set for November 18, 2026; whether Huang will attend remains unclear. The letter also allows for Huang to set an alternative date during while the 119th Congress is still in session.On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed. It is alleged that the latter was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information and help China get its hands on Nvidia's AI GPUs, the most powerful of which are banned from export to the country by Washington. Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion of AI chips into China. You may like Nvidia's Jensen Huang officially called to Congress due to reports of a Chinese spy plot US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to having an affair with suspected Chinese spy In a statement to Nvidia employees, Jensen Huang said, "To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." As Huang's statement noted, Nvidia has opened an independent investigation into its CEO's conduct regarding the national security concerns the story has laid bare. The board of directors stated, "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."Nvidia shares dropped by around 5% in early trading, but have since recovered some of their losses. The company has rocketed to a market capitalization of over $4 trillion as the global hardware leader of the AI boom. history.titleZh: 英伟达CEO黄仁勋因与疑似中国间谍有染被传唤至国会
history.descriptionZh:
美国众议院中国问题特别委员会等三个委员会的主席已联名致函英伟达CEO黄仁勋，要求其出席联合闭门简报，说明英伟达防范外国对手间谍活动的安全协议，以及他与新加坡数据中心公司Megaspeed高管Alice Huang的往来。信件由众议员Brian J. Mast、John Moolenaar和Eric A. Crawford签署，闭门听证会定于2026年11月18日举行；黄仁勋是否出席尚不清楚，信中还允许其在第119届国会会期内另定日期。委员会称，有关黄仁勋与Alice Huang婚外情的报道引发“重大国家安全担忧”，涉及中国获取美国敏感技术和信息；中国渗透并获取美国尖端技术是这三个委员会本届国会调查工作的核心，国会需要确定美国国家安全受到多大程度的风险。

事件背景是，黄仁勋在不到24小时前承认与Alice Huang有婚外情。Alice Huang曾任新加坡Megaspeed高管，被公开报道为与中国情报有关联的人员。相关指控称，她由中国国家安全部招募，负责搜集信息并帮助中国获得英伟达AI GPU，而华盛顿禁止向中国出口英伟达最强大的AI芯片。Megaspeed还被指控将价值20亿美元的AI芯片走私到中国。黄仁勋在致英伟达员工的声明中承认对妻子不忠，并向家人和同事道歉，称“没有借口”。英伟达已就CEO行为及由此暴露的国家安全担忧启动独立调查，董事会表示，目前没有理由认为国家安全或英伟达机密受到损害，但调查将审查所有可用信息。

从技术背景看，英伟达GPU是当前AI大模型训练和推理的核心硬件，广泛应用于数据中心、生成式AI和高性能计算。美国出口管制针对的是最先进AI芯片，目的是限制中国获得可用于军事和战略竞争的高端算力。此次争议的核心并非英伟达发布新产品或技术原理创新，而是高端AI GPU出口管制可能被规避、企业安全协议是否足以防范外国情报渗透，以及高管与外国情报相关人员接触带来的合规和国家安全风险。原文未披露涉事GPU的具体型号、算力、内存带宽等性能参数，因此无法进行具体性能对比；可确认的关键数据包括：Megaspeed被指走私20亿美元AI芯片，英伟达市值超过4万亿美元，消息公布后股价早盘一度下跌约5%，随后部分收复跌幅。

该事件可能对英伟达产生多方面影响：国会调查将审视其出口合规、内部安全和高管风险管理；英伟达的独立调查结果可能影响其与国会及监管机构的关系；在地缘政治和AI芯片出口管制趋严的背景下，市场也会关注事件是否波及英伟达在中国及全球AI硬件供应链中的业务。应用层面，英伟达GPU主要用于AI模型训练、推理和大型数据中心部署，是当前全球AI基础设施的关键组件。事件仍在发展中，黄仁勋是否出席听证会、国会将获取哪些信息以及英伟达调查结论，均有待观察。

history.title: Bizarre AI chip demo uses butter to highlight how new chip runs 40 degrees cooler than the competition
history.description: DEEPX demonstrated its DX-M1 processor’s cool running capabilities in a bizarre dairy-based thermal benchmark.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Processors generating excess heat play a significant part in contemporary data center design, cost, and resource use. However, things could be vastly different if AI chips were more efficient and ran far cooler. South Korean chip startup DEEPX, recently featured by CNBC, thinks its AI chip designs are the answer. DEEPX demonstrated its DX-M1 processor’s cool-running capabilities in a bizarre new dairy-based thermal benchmark. While rival chips caused a knob of butter to sizzle in seconds, atop the DEEPX solution, the butter block remains solid.Concerns over AI data center proliferation are growing worldwide. These developments are shaping business, the environment, and politics. Some people have very strong feelings about them, and hundreds of people have risked being thrown into jail protesting data centers. The CNBC report linked in the intro looks into why modern data centers are problematic, and indicates that the core issues stem from the use of hot-running processors and the extensive power and cooling apparatus they need.DEEPX says its simple answer is to “make the AI chips themselves run cooler.” The CNBC video includes a demo of the ultra-low-power DX-M1 processor. In a side-by-side test against unnamed rival AI chips, you can see the DX-M1 NPU is clearly cooler. DEEPX CEO Kim Nok-won claims a temperature difference of 25 to more than 40 degrees Celsius compared with competitors. Kim said the side-by-side chips processed “the same AI workload… and every chip melted the butter except the last chip [DX-M1].”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The dairy-based thermal challenge is certainly eyebrow-raising, but we note some big gaps in the comparison information. Most notable was the question of how fast each processor tackles the test workload. Anyone can run a chip cool if the power and clocks are scaled back. PC enthusiasts undervolt and/or underclock their GPUs all the time for efficiency, better thermals, and reduced fan noise.DEEPX’s DX-M1 NPU has been produced on Samsung 5nm since August 2025, according to The Elec reports. It has won approximately $13.3M worth of orders thanks to this sliver of silicon. The company is planning to move forward with the next-gen DX-M2 AI chip, which is based on Samsung 2nm, with its mass production aiming for H2 2027. You may like ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC OpenAI’s 700W Jalapeño ASIC outpaces 1,400W Nvidia flagship GPU Software could be the easiest fix for hyperscalers' AI power squeeze, researchers say In conclusion, these NPUs look set for edge computing and robotics applications, so they aren’t really competing in the same space as the racks of power-gulping Nvidia Blackwell and Ruben GPUs featured in the CNBC news feature. Eventually, we might see the hundreds or thousands of hot-running Nvidia GPUs with beefy liquid cooling apparatus get replaced by cooler-running custom accelerators. Such an innovation could cool the backlash against AI data centers. However, DEEPX’s DX-M1 or even DX-M2 chips aren’t going to compete in that space, so this butter test is a bit of a red herring.The CNBC report also highlights SK hynix’s work on iHBM, a next-gen low-power consumption, and cool-running. The ‘i’ stands for ‘Integrated Cooling Element,’ according to an exec talking to CNBC.
